INSTRUCTIONS.TITLE: About Visual Analysis
INSTRUCTIONS.INTRO: This module lets you inspect the invariant-mass results collected by students in a selected session.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_1: Choose a session from the dropdown above the Results table.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_2: The Mass Histograms show the combined distribution of particle masses reported by the selected students.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_3: In the Results table, select or deselect students to include or exclude their data from the histograms.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_4: Use the refresh button if new student results become available.
INSTRUCTIONS.HOW_TO_READ_INTRO: Each histogram shows the invariant mass of a candidate particle:
INSTRUCTIONS.CLEAR_PEAK: A clear peak indicates that students correctly identified that particle.
INSTRUCTIONS.BROAD_DISTRIBUTION: A broad or flat distribution may mean misidentification or too few candidates.
INSTRUCTIONS.TIP: Compare histograms across students or sessions to see how consistently the class reconstructed each particle species.

INSTRUCTIONS.TITLE: About Large Scale Analysis
INSTRUCTIONS.INTRO: This module combines results from a masterclass event to study strangeness enhancement - how the production of strange particles increases in heavy-ion Pb-Pb collisions relative to proton-proton collisions.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_1: Choose an event from the dropdown above the plot.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_2: The plot shows strangeness enhancement as a function of collision centrality, measured by No. participants.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_3: The Results table lists yields and enhancement values for each centrality class and particle species.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_4: Use the refresh button if new results become available.
INSTRUCTIONS.YIELD_DEF: efficiency-corrected yield per event: reconstructed particle count divided by (number of analysed events × reconstruction efficiency)
INSTRUCTIONS.NPART_DEF: average number of nucleons participating in the collision
INSTRUCTIONS.NO_PARTICLE_DEF: average student signal from the Large Scale Analysis fit for that centrality class and particle species: excess of counts over the combinatorial background under the peak
INSTRUCTIONS.ENHANCEMENT_DEF: yield per participant, normalised to a pp reference:
INSTRUCTIONS.WHERE_YPP: where Ypp is the reference yield in pp collisions.
INSTRUCTIONS.FACTOR_TWO: The factor 2 converts the pp yield to a per-participant scale, since a pp collision involves two protons.

INSTRUCTIONS.LOOK_FOR_END: Discuss with students why denser collisions may produce more strange quarks.
INSTRUCTIONS.TIP: Use the coloured markers in the table together with the plot to connect a specific centrality class to its point on the graph.

INSTRUCTIONS.TITLE: About R_AA Analysis
INSTRUCTIONS.INTRO: This module combines the J/psi yields students measured in pp, p-Pb and Pb-Pb collisions into the nuclear modification factor RAA - a measure of how J/psi production in Pb-Pb collisions is suppressed or enhanced relative to a simple superposition of independent proton-proton collisions.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_1: Choose an event from the dropdown above the plot.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_2: The plot shows R_AA as a function of collision centrality, measured by No. participants, for the eight Pb-Pb centrality classes.
INSTRUCTIONS.STEP_3: The Results table lists every collision system a student analysed, with the raw signal, Acc × ε, corrected yield and, for Pb-Pb, R_AA.
INSTRUCTIONS.NO_JPSI_DEF: the fitted J/psi signal from the residual-fit yield extraction (unlike-sign minus like-sign pairs), with its Poisson error
INSTRUCTIONS.EFFICIENCY_DEF: the full acceptance × efficiency (A × ε, including PID) for that collision system - centrality-dependent for Pb-Pb, flat for pp and p-Pb
INSTRUCTIONS.YIELD_DEF: the Acc × ε-corrected yield per event (as measured by the student; for pp this is still at 7 TeV):
INSTRUCTIONS.NCOLL_DEF: average number of binary nucleon-nucleon collisions in that centrality class (Glauber Monte Carlo)
INSTRUCTIONS.RAA_DEF: the Pb-Pb yield divided by what Ncoll independent pp collisions would have produced, using an energy-rescaled pp reference:
INSTRUCTIONS.ENERGY_NOTE: The student pp sample is at 7 TeV, while Pb-Pb is at 5.02 TeV. The Yield column still shows the student Acc × ε-corrected pp yield. For RAA only, that yield is multiplied by f7→5.02 ≈ 0.82 (ratio of published midrapidity J/ψ cross sections at 5.02 and 7 TeV), so student results still drive event-to-event differences while the absolute RAA scale matches a same-energy reference.
INSTRUCTIONS.LOOK_FOR: R_AA below 1 indicates suppression of J/psi production in Pb-Pb collisions (e.g. from colour screening in the quark-gluon plasma); R_AA above 1 would indicate enhancement. The p-Pb row is shown for reference only and does not enter the R_AA calculation.
INSTRUCTIONS.TIP: The dashed line on the plot marks R_AA = 1, i.e. no nuclear modification.
